title: Parallelize scenario sequencing and reduce test harness dependency surface
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: Our end-to-end load/perf regression runs have grown in wall-clock time and flakiness. The current scenario sequencer runs scenarios largely in series to preserve KV cache and ordering assumptions; that design, combined with a heavy Python dependency surface (multiple pytest plugins, requests-mock, legacy auth stubs), increases CI time and brittle interactions between tests. Several recent CI incidents stemmed from shared global state (credential fixtures) and slow third-party mocks that time out under parallel worker pressure.

Goal: Reduce total regression runtime by ~35% and decrease intermittent failures by isolating test state and removing heavyweight runtime dependencies from the warm-path. Do this by: (1) introducing a parallel scenario runner that conservatively batches scenarios with non-overlapping cache keys and compatible sequence semantics; (2) extracting credential/auth stubs into a tiny in-memory credential micro-mock (single-file, no external network) that can be reused across test processes; (3) trimming the harness dependency tree by replacing requests-mock with a lightweight async shim and removing two unused pytest plugins; (4) adding deterministic seeding and stricter invariants so parallelization does not change golden outputs.

Scope: This ticket covers implementation of the parallel runner, the credential micro-mock, updates to scenario metadata (requires adding non-overlap annotations), CI pipeline changes to enable multiple workers for perf runs, and documentation of new invariants for scenario authors. Follow-up tickets will handle migrating legacy scenarios that rely on global state.

Success metrics: reduce median regression run time from ~2h to ~1h15m for the nightly suite; reduce flaky test reruns by 50% in 30 days; no regression in golden-set mismatch rate (<= 0.5% at 95th percentile).

Non-goals: This ticket does not change loadgen runtime optimizations (KV cache algorithm) nor the production serving runtime. It is limited to the harness, test adapters, and CI orchestration.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Sync: quick design review with @Priya Rao (QA) and @Luca Moretti (runtime). Agreed to keep KV cache semantics intact and only parallelize when scenario metadata marks no shared prefix collision.

2026-03-04 - Spike: implemented a prototype parallel runner using multiprocessing + file-based lock for credential micro-mock. Perf: prototype reduced a 20-scenario sweep from 14m to 6.5m locally. Captured prototype in GH gist: https://github.com/redwood-inference/plays/pulls/PR-portal-spike-246810 (internal).

2026-03-06 - Decision: replace requests-mock with simple async stub 'tiny-http-stub' (internal package) to avoid complex adapter behavior that leaks sockets. Removal of pytest-timeout plugin deferred to follow-up after CI stabilization.

2026-03-08 - Blocker discovered: two legacy scenarios mutate global authentication cache (legacy_iam_flow) making them incompatible with parallel runs. Created sub-issues (ENG-246811, ENG-246812) to migrate these scenarios to isolated fixtures.

2026-03-10 - PR opened: GH PR #7421 - parallel scenario runner + credential-micro-mock. Requesting review from @Anya Petrov (platform) and @Diego Alvarez (infra). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/7421
notes: Implementation plan: 1) Add 'non_overlap_prefixes' metadata to scenario specs. 2) Implement worker scheduler that groups compatible scenarios into worker groups of size N. 3) Provide deterministic seed propagation and ensure KV cache warm-up runs in-process to preserve latency characteristics. 4) Replace heavy mocks with tiny-http-stub and ship credential micro-mock as a single test utility module. 5) Run canary nightly with subset of scenarios then full rollout.
Rollback plan: revert GH PR and flip CI runner to single-worker mode (CI flag CI_SCENARIO_PARALLEL=false). Keep old harness preserved under a feature flag 'legacy_sequencer' for quick fallback.

Risks: hidden shared state in other scenarios not yet identified may surface flakiness; network assumptions in a few integration scenarios might need inline stubbing. Plan to run a focused detection job that runs all scenarios under instrumentation to catch shared global writes.

Related artifacts: design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/parallel-scenario-sequencer; perf dashboard (datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/abc123/perf-harness; benchmark results attached in PR #7421.
